title: Prime extremality and stability for weighted primitive sets
abstract: A set of integers greater than one is primitive if no member divides another. We prove Kucheriaviy's conjecture that the primes maximize the sum of z^Ω(n) / [n (log n)^z] over primitive sets for every 0 < z ≤ 1, where Ω counts prime factors with multiplicity. The primes are the unique maximizer throughout this interval and remain so through z = 4/3. For 0 < z ≤ 1, the loss in the sum is at least a positive multiple of the weight of the symmetric difference from the primes. The best such multiple is asymptotic to κz² as z tends to zero from above. We give a formula for κ involving a supremum of convergent prime sums and show that it rounds to 0.41123. To obtain κ, it suffices to consider replacements that keep the primes below a cutoff and exchange the remaining primes for the semiprimes they generate. A prime can nevertheless be outweighed in its own least-prime-factor class. For infinitely many primes p, the semiprimes with least prime factor p outweigh p for every sufficiently small z, depending on p. The proof of the conjecture reweights Alexeev's divisibility flow for the classical Erdős sum.
teaser: The primes uniquely maximize the weighted primitive-set sum on the full conjectured interval. The optimal stability constant has quadratic order at zero, with a leading coefficient that rounds to 0.41123.

title: Switch distance and the central spectral gap of cubic graphs
abstract: Guo and Royle classified the cubic graphs whose adjacency spectra avoid the open interval (-1,1). We show that the number of eigenvalues in this interval measures how far a cubic graph is from their class. Let G be a finite simple cubic graph on n ≠ 6 vertices, and let k count its adjacency eigenvalues strictly between -1 and 1, with multiplicity. The minimum number of degree-preserving edge switches needed to reach the class on the same vertex set lies between k/2 and Ck, for an absolute constant C. In the bipartite double of the components that need repair, disjoint paths of four-cycles cover all but O(k) vertices and have O(k) ends in total, regardless of their lengths. As a consequence, every growing family of cubic graphs with uniformly positive edge expansion has a positive proportion of its eigenvalues strictly inside the interval.
teaser: For simple cubic graphs on a number of vertices different from six, the number of eigenvalues inside (−1,1) controls, up to absolute constants, the edge-switch distance to graphs whose spectra avoid that interval.
description: For simple cubic graphs on a number of vertices different from six, the number of eigenvalues inside (−1,1) controls, up to absolute constants, the edge-switch distance to graphs whose spectra avoid that interval.

title: Periodic solutions and decidability for signed integer tilings
abstract: Let f be a finitely supported integer function on ℤ^d and g a fully periodic integer function. We prove that whenever f * a = g has a bounded integer solution, it has a fully periodic integer solution. Bounded integer solvability is decidable in every finite dimension. These results answer two questions of Greenfeld and Tao. More precisely, given a finite set containing the support of f and a scalar period of g, one can compute a single finite torus on which solvability can be tested for all choices of the coefficients of f and the values of g. The proof uses torsion cosets of the convolution symbol to describe the fractional parts of homogeneous corrections. On parallel lattice slices these residues form compact groups. A periodic choice of residues lifts to an integer solution with the prescribed right-hand side.
teaser: A bounded integer solution of a finite convolution equation with a periodic right-hand side guarantees a fully periodic integer solution. Solvability is decidable in every finite dimension.

title: Local crystal order from small low-frequency scattering in dimensions 8 and 24
abstract: Cohen, Cohn and Viazovska identified the particle arrangements that suppress scattering over the widest possible frequency ball in dimensions 8 and 24. We prove a stability theorem that allows positive scattering throughout that ball. Suppose a stationary particle process of intensity one has finite local second moments and covariance spectral mass at most δ inside the open ball up to the first reciprocal shell of E₈ or the Leech lattice. With probability tending to one, every particle in an observation ball of radius comparable to log(1/δ)/log log(1/δ) can be matched to a distinct site of one isometric copy of the corresponding lattice inside the same ball. Each displacement is O_a(δ^a) for every fixed 0 < a < 1/12, and the fraction of vacant sites tends to zero. No minimum particle separation is assumed. The proof converts spectral mass into a bound on close pairs and applies the packing stability theorem of Böröczky, Radchenko and Ramos. For periodic configurations the hypothesis is a sum of squared density amplitudes of the kind minimized in collective-coordinate simulations.
teaser: In dimensions 8 and 24, small low-frequency scattering forces particle configurations close to a copy of the E₈ or Leech lattice on growing observation balls, under the stated stationary-process hypotheses.

title: Reconfiguring Hamiltonian paths in complete joins
abstract: When can one Hamiltonian path be transformed into another by rotations at its ends? We answer this question for the complete join of two nonempty graphs. If one part has d ≥ 1 more vertices than the other, the connected components of the rotation graph correspond bijectively to the components of a graph of (d − 1)-edge linear forests in the larger part, with one edge exchanged at each step. Whenever a Hamiltonian path exists and the part sizes differ by at most five, the rotation graph is connected and its diameter has linear order in the number of vertices. Together with Kazazi’s examples, this makes six the first imbalance at which connectivity can fail. For joins on n vertices of minimum degree at least n/2, we also obtain connectivity when d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 9d − 14. A planar example gives the exact temporary increase in the maximum leg length needed to transform one tour into another by depot-incident edits.

title: Logarithmic regularity and Fourier uniqueness on compressed square-root grids
abstract: When do the values of a function and its Fourier transform determine the function? We study this question on the grids Λβ = {0} ∪ {±√n/[log(e+n)]ᵝ for n ≥ 1}. For α > 1, let Xα consist of functions whose squared absolute values, and those of their Fourier transforms, are integrable with weight (1 + |x|)[log(e + |x|)]^α. If β > 1/2, simultaneous vanishing on the grid forces zero in every Xα. If 0 ≤ β < 1/2, every fixed Xα contains an infinite-dimensional real space of even Fourier-invariant functions with the prescribed zeros. On the critical grid β = 1/2, uniqueness holds for α ≥ 3/2, including equality, while the construction of Bondarenko and Seip gives nonuniqueness for α > 1 sufficiently close to 1. Thus uniqueness on the union of Xα over α > 1 holds exactly when β > 1/2. The proof combines a constrained Neumann spectral estimate with the Kulikov–Nazarov–Sodin localization method, and extends the Bondarenko–Seip kernel estimates to an enlarged tail. The exact critical regularity on β = 1/2 remains open. The results concern exact infinite sampling; no stability or finite-data reconstruction claim is made.

title: Sharp constants for bounded ratios of rank-two Lorentzian matrices
abstract: Huang, Huh, Soskin and Wang characterized bounded ratios of Lorentzian matrix entries by cut inequalities. We prove that every normalized bounded ratio has supremum at most two on matrices of rank at most two. The supremum equals two exactly when the indices admit an ordering in which every proper initial cut is tight. In particular, the seven-index ratio that exceeds two in Zhou's rank-three example has rank-two supremum exactly two. We prove the coefficientwise conjecture of Huang, Huh, Soskin and Wang for all integral hypermetric exponents and find the optimal multiplier eight for each of the two six-index hypermetrics they single out. For bounded integral ratios whose denominator uses each edge of the complete bipartite graph K(2,N) once, we compute both the numerical supremum and the least coefficientwise multiplier. For every bounded integral ratio, the kth root of the least coefficientwise multiplier for its kth power converges to the rank-two numerical supremum of the original ratio.

title: A mixing lower bound for the Pólya-tree Burnside sampler
abstract: Bartholdi and Diaconis observed that several statistics of their sampler for uniform unlabeled rooted trees appeared to stabilize after about twenty sweeps from a star. We prove that the tree retains a trace of this initial symmetry in large families of identical branches. For every fixed 0 < c < √(8/π), after ⌊c√(log n)⌋ sweeps from the centered star on n vertices, the total variation distance from the uniform law tends to one as n grows. Even the expected width after any fixed number of sweeps exceeds its stationary mean by a factor tending to infinity. The proof uses large prime divisors of random permutation orders to carry a lower bound on branch multiplicity from one tree to the next.

title: The chi-square mixing order of fixed-alphabet Burnside chains
abstract: We determine the order of the worst-start chi-square mixing time of the coordinate-permutation Burnside chain on words of length n over a fixed alphabet. For every fixed k ≥ 3, the upper bound is O(n/log n), matching the known lower order. More generally, for the twisted chain with fixed cycle-weight parameter θ > 0, chi-square distance tends to zero uniformly over all labeled starting words at time ⌈cn/log n⌉ whenever c > log k/(2θ). The proof uses the established representation by products of stochastic matrices with independent Dirichlet rows. A bound on the probability that two rows have small overlap gives polynomial decay of all moments of the Dobrushin coefficient. Inserting these estimates into the trace expansion yields a stationary-average bound that decays faster than every inverse polynomial. Coordinate symmetry then gives the uniform starting-state bound.

title: Exact entropy constants for balanced multislices
abstract: Consider the uniform measure μ on words with m colours, each appearing r times, and assign unit weight to every unordered pair of coordinates. If Q(f) is the sum of the pair conditional entropies, we prove that the largest coefficient κ in κ Ent_μ(f) ≤ Q(f) is binom(m,2) r² log 2 / log((mr)!/(r!)^m). A singleton indicator attains equality. This establishes the balanced case of the multicolour formula proposed by Bristiel and Caputo and determines the optimal logarithmic edge-expansion coefficient of the associated transposition graph. The proof combines their exact Bernoulli–Laplace entropy constant with Salez's conditioning on the complete position set of one colour. Equal multiplicities make the resulting induction close without loss. We also record the resulting classical log-Sobolev bounds and give a self-contained proof of the known binary input.

title: Removing the logarithmic loss in a lower bound for sum-difference exponents
abstract: For a finite rational slope family containing 0, 1 and ∞, the sum-difference exponent measures how much entropy an output projection can have relative to the largest input projection entropy. Tao bounded this exponent from below by 2 − Oₖ(log(2 + D)/D), where D is the rational complexity of the output relative to the inputs and k is the number of additional input slopes. For k ≥ 1, we prove the lower bound 2 − Cₖ/D, with an explicit constant depending only on k. The proof retains Tao's evaluated-polynomial construction and adds a covering estimate between two comparable degree-and-coefficient scales. This estimate holds for sets of evaluated values, including when polynomial evaluations coincide. A separate appendix evaluates the corrected folded-entropy functional associated with the three-slope continuous limit. Its infimum is log(2/√3) for every folding parameter, by the classical sharp entropy Brascamp–Lieb inequality and concentration into a single strip.

title: Certifying conditional dependence among environmental records from CHSH correlations
abstract: Environmental records can be individually accurate while sharing the same errors. We show how retained coherence can quantify this conditional dependence without reconstructing the joint record distribution. For a balanced two-qubit state supported on span{|00⟩, |11⟩}, we derive the sharp compatibility boundary between a retained Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) value, the accuracy of R designated local binary records, and their conditional total correlation. The full extremum reduces to a convex problem in R + 1 Hamming-weight probabilities, and every boundary value has a pure-state quantum realization using only the designated fragments. Its inverse gives the least dependence compatible with Bell data and separate record calibrations. For two records it is explicit; at fixed accuracy, a fixed positive Bell excess requires dependence growing at least linearly with record count. Independent monitoring reaches the zero-dependence boundary in a Lindblad dephasing limit. A shared-memory Lindblad process instead improves record accuracy at constant Bell value, with an exact time after which dependence becomes certifiable. The result quantifies departures from conditional independence in environmental recording, under trusted state-sector and readout assumptions.

title: A Gumbel law for Markovian super-coupon collection
abstract: An r-element subset of an n-element universe evolves by replacing a uniformly chosen element with a uniformly chosen element outside the current set. Each configuration collects all of its s-element subsets. For every fixed pair 2 ≤ s < r, we prove that the expected time to collect all s-subsets is asymptotic to [C(n,s)/C(r−1,s−1)] log C(n,s), where C(a,b) denotes a binomial coefficient. This proves the fixed-parameter off-diagonal case of the conjecture of Athreya, Mukherjee and Mukherjee. We also obtain a Poisson limit for the number of subsets still missing near completion and a standard Gumbel limit for the centered and scaled collection time. The conclusions hold from every initial configuration. The proof controls joint avoidance of any fixed family of target subsets, uniformly over their overlaps. Restricting the walk to the labels in that family gives a finite transition matrix, and a stationary-flow identity determines its leading killing rate. Standard spectral and factorial-moment arguments then give the collection-time limits.
teaser: The paper proves the fixed-parameter off-diagonal collection-time conjecture and gives Poisson and Gumbel limits for the one-swap model.
description: The paper proves the fixed-parameter off-diagonal collection-time conjecture and gives Poisson and Gumbel limits for the one-swap model.

title: Proximal approximation of firmly nonexpansive maps with small derivative asymmetry
abstract: We study uniform approximation of a firmly nonexpansive map by the proximal map of a single convex function. Let H be a real Hilbert space, let R > 0, and suppose that T is continuously Fréchet differentiable on a neighbourhood of the closed ball B_{√2R}, firmly nonexpansive on that ball, and satisfies sup_{B_{√2R}} ‖DT−DT*‖ ≤ ε. We prove that a finite continuous convex function φ exists with sup_{B_R} ‖T−prox_φ‖ ≤ R√(2ε). The estimate is independent of dimension and requires no bound on derivatives of the skew part. The proof converts the differential defect into approximate convex interpolation inequalities, then applies an elementary form of established approximate-subdifferential integration. An affine proximal approximation gives the complementary bound R/2. For a planar rotation perturbation with 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1, the exact approximation error is εR/2; thus this example does not establish optimality of the square-root rate.
teaser: A dimension-independent bound approximates a firmly nonexpansive map by one convex proximal map when the derivative is nearly symmetric.
description: A dimension-independent bound approximates a firmly nonexpansive map by one convex proximal map when the derivative is nearly symmetric.

title: Catalyst-rank limits for second-order entanglement concentration
abstract: Exact catalysts can improve the second-order yield of pure-state entanglement concentration, but the optimal yield does not specify how the catalyst must grow. We obtain a necessary rank condition for this improvement. Let the source have a fixed nonuniform finite squared Schmidt vector, with entropy H and information variance V defined using base-two logarithms, and fix a required squared fidelity q ∈ (0,1). For pure outputs of n source copies, with a pure catalyst returned exactly and uncorrelated, suppose that the target contains nH+b√n+o(√n) Bell pairs. If the catalyst rank K_n satisfies lim sup log₂ K_n/√n ≤ c<∞, we give an explicit necessary fidelity bound strictly below e^{-b^2/(2V)} for every b>0. Consequently, attaining the known unrestricted coefficient √(2V ln(1/q)) requires log₂ K_n/√n → ∞. Catalysts with log₂ K_n=o(√n) cannot improve the unassisted coefficient. The proof combines a fidelity concentration estimate, a Gaussian limit of the majorization inequalities, and a positive tail term retained by the rank constraint.
teaser: The paper bounds the Schmidt rank needed for exact entanglement catalysis to achieve the optimal second-order concentration yield.
description: The paper bounds the Schmidt rank needed for exact entanglement catalysis to achieve the optimal second-order concentration yield.
abstract_tex: Exact catalysts can improve the second-order yield of pure-state entanglement concentration, but the optimal yield does not specify how the catalyst must grow. We obtain a necessary rank condition for this improvement. Let the source have a fixed nonuniform finite squared Schmidt vector, with entropy \(H\) and information variance \(V\) defined using base-two logarithms, and fix a required squared fidelity \(q\in(0,1)\). For pure outputs of \(n\) source copies, with a pure catalyst returned exactly and uncorrelated, suppose that the target contains \(nH+b\sqrt n+o(\sqrt n)\) Bell pairs. If the catalyst rank \(K_n\) satisfies \(\limsup \log_2K_n/\sqrt n\le c<\infty\), we give an explicit necessary fidelity bound strictly below \(e^{-b^2/(2V)}\) for every \(b>0\). Consequently, attaining the known unrestricted coefficient \(\sqrt{2V\ln(1/q)}\) requires \(\log_2K_n/\sqrt n\to\infty\). Catalysts with \(\log_2K_n=o(\sqrt n)\) cannot improve the unassisted coefficient. The proof combines a fidelity concentration estimate, a Gaussian limit of the majorization inequalities, and a positive tail term retained by the rank constraint.

title: Integral homology of strong Morse matching complexes of cycles
abstract: We determine the reduced integral homology of the full strong discrete Morse matching complex of every cycle. Apart from the five-cycle, the answer is the sum of two free abelian contributions whose degrees and ranks follow explicit formulas according to the cycle order modulo four and modulo three. The proof represents a pairing by two local order inequalities. Their conflict graph is a regular bipartite graph with a known independence complex; the strong matching complex is obtained by removing exactly two families of monochromatic vertex covers. The resulting relative chain complex splits into two copies of a simplex relative to the noncover complex of the cycle. Combinatorial Alexander duality and the long exact sequence then give the homology in all orders, extending the finite calculations of Knudson and Owens-White. The same face description gives a transfer-matrix formula for the face polynomial and a twelve-periodic reduced Euler characteristic.
teaser: The paper computes the integral homology of strong Morse matching complexes for all cycles and gives a transfer-matrix formula for their face polynomials.

title: A sharp refresh scale for power-free interval counts
abstract: The random-sieve model of power-free integers assigns an independent uniform forbidden residue class modulo p^k to each prime p. We determine how the centered count in an interval of length H responds when each prime coordinate is independently resampled with probability ε_H. For every fixed integer k ≥ 2, the correlation between the original and resampled counts tends to e^{-t} when ε_Hlog log H → t ∈ [0,∞), and tends to zero when this product diverges. Thus 1/log log H is the sharp refresh scale. The proof expresses the covariance as a positive arithmetic sum and transfers the classical normal order of the number of distinct prime factors to its bounded weights. An exact cancellation of Euler factors then gives the correlation profile. As a consequence, the number of prime coordinates in a character sampled according to the interval count's normalized Fourier energy, divided by log log H, converges in probability to one.
teaser: A random sieve for power-free integers has a sharp resampling scale. The paper determines the limiting correlation between the original and resampled interval counts.

title: Interpreting Recovery in Human–Robot Affinity
abstract: A response to a robot can return above its initial level even while an adverse contribution continues to grow. Interpreting such recovery requires distinguishing what a trajectory can exclude from what it can identify. We examine models in which the same positive process contributes to the response and drives an opponent through fixed nonnegative filtering. With zero history, fixed positive observation weights and a log-concave positive driver, the opponent-to-driver ratio cannot decrease, so a return above baseline after a negative excursion is impossible. The argument applies to arbitrary nonnegative delay mixtures and includes a published isolated-dose opponent architecture under its actual decaying input. A saturating two-state construction illustrates one way to escape the restriction while both contributions increase. Fixed nondecreasing scalar observation maps preserve the strict crossing diagnostic, whereas arithmetic averaging need not: an exact example has a recovering mean although neither individual recovers. These conditional comparisons clarify how individual trajectories, exposure history and observation assumptions enter model selection. The examples are synthetic and do not validate a psychological interpretation of the latent states.
teaser: A conceptual companion examines what recovery in human–robot affinity can exclude or identify under explicit model and observation assumptions, and why a recovering average need not imply individual recovery.

title: A Newton-face criterion for finite-state categorical Bernoulli factories
abstract: Let a deterministic finite-state machine read independent samples from an unknown categorical distribution with full support and stop almost surely with a binary output. We characterize the rational target probabilities that such a machine can realize. Write the target as P/Q, where P and Q are coprime homogeneous polynomials of the same degree with rational coefficients and 0<P<Q on the positive orthant. A finite-state factory exists if and only if every nonempty Newton-face polynomial of both P and Q-P is strictly positive on the positive orthant. Whenever this condition holds, a fixed-block restart factory exists. The criterion is decidable by real quantifier elimination, and a successful test leads to an exact construction. The proof combines a Markov-chain tree representation of the two output probabilities, Handelman's positive-multiple theorem and the block construction of Mossel and Peres. Examples explain why the complementary numerator is essential and why powers of the coordinate sum do not exhaust the possible multipliers. No bound on decision complexity, block length or state count is asserted.

title: Sharp entropy retention under edge deletion in roses and parallel-edge graphs
abstract: Let a finite graph have strictly positive edge lengths, and let its entropy be the exponential growth rate of reduced circuits per unit metric length. We determine the smallest possible fraction of entropy retained by an optimal one-edge deletion for two graph families. For a rose with r >= 3 loops, this fraction is log(2r - 3)/log(2r - 1). For two vertices joined by k >= 4 parallel edges, it is log(k - 2)/log(k - 1). In each family, deleting any longest edge is optimal, and equality in the sharp bound holds exactly when all edge lengths are equal. The rose result proves the sharp three-loop bound and the uniform lower bound conjectured by Hamed, Aougab and Clay. The proof uses scalar Perron equations for entropy, a change of variables to a concave logistic-power function, and concentration of coordinates under a fixed-sum constraint. Repeated deletion gives sharp bounds for retaining several edges.

title: A commutator estimate for the Golden–Thompson gap in qubit chains
status_note: A HAL deposit was awaiting moderation on 2 November 2026; a public HAL record has not yet been confirmed.
abstract: For a finite qubit chain with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions, split the interaction sum into its odd and even bond layers A and B. We compare the logarithmic trace gap F(β) = log{τ(e^(βA)e^(βB))/τ(e^(β(A+B)))} with E = τ([A,B]*[A,B]), where τ is the normalized trace. If every bond has operator norm at most J, then β⁴E/48 ≤ F(β) ≤ β⁴E/16 for 0 ≤ βJ ≤ 1/16000. The constants and interval are independent of chain length and remain valid when local commutator contributions nearly cancel. The proof retains two occurrences of the full commutator in an ordered-cumulant expansion before applying local estimates. A spanning-tree bound and a matrix row-and-column estimate then control the full Taylor remainder relative to E. The result gives a one-step partition-function certificate and a converse on the stated high-temperature interval. An exactly solvable four-site example illustrates the role of cancellation.
abstract_tex: For a finite qubit chain with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions, split the interaction sum into its odd and even bond layers \(A\) and \(B\). teaser: A two-sided estimate controls the Golden–Thompson gap in a qubit chain at high temperature. The bounds depend on the commutator of the two bond layers and hold uniformly in the chain length.

title: Convergence and finite length of the Brascamp–Lieb scaling flow
abstract: We give a proof of full convergence of the prescribed Brascamp–Lieb scaling flow for every feasible real datum with positive real weights, answering Question 2.10 of Bez, Gauvan, and Tsuji. The limit is geometric, and the sequence of complete scaling iterations has finite length in the product Frobenius norm. Stacking the matrices with square-root weights identifies the two normalizations with nearest-point projections onto a product of scaled row-Stiefel manifolds and a column-Stiefel manifold. The result then follows from the asymptotic normalization theorem of Bez, Gauvan, and Tsuji and the established local alternating-projection theory of Noll and Rondepierre. We also give a direct verification of the descent conditions of Attouch, Bolte, and Svaiter. The one-dimensional-output recurrence agrees with the prescribed-norm frame algorithm studied by Zhu and Li. An explicit feasible example has infinite interleaved half-step length and error of order k^(-1/2), clarifying the scope of the complete-iteration conclusion.

title: A dimension-independent spectral rounding bound for orthogonal synchronization
abstract: Spectral methods for orthogonal synchronization relax the orthogonality constraints and round the blocks to the orthogonal group. We bound the objective value after this rounding in terms of the spectral relaxation. On any finite connected weighted graph with labels in O(r), let γ be the normalized scalar Laplacian gap and let Λᵣ be the sum of the lowest r normalized connection Laplacian eigenvalues. Nearest-orthogonal rounding of the degree-normalized bottom spectral frame gives normalized squared-Frobenius frustration ν(Q) ≤ (3 + 12/γ)Λᵣ/r. The coefficient is independent of r and depends on the graph only through γ. The proof controls the positive magnitudes of the spectral blocks through a classical matrix absolute-value inequality, graph Poincaré and the frame’s second-moment normalization. We compare this certificate with the dimension-dependent connection-Cheeger bound and two dimension-independent optimum-relative estimates: a Frobenius perturbation deduction with graph dependence and a comparison using the next connection eigenvalue. No closeness to a consistent assignment is assumed.

title: A uniform logarithmic lower bound for cyclovariety Mahler measures
abstract: Let Cₖ be the cyclovariety associated with all k-th roots of unity in the construction of Cornelissen, Hokken and Ringeling. We prove, for every integer k ≥ 2, m(Cₖ) ≥ (1/6) log k − 1/4 + 1/(3k) − 1/(12k²). Together with the known upper bound, this gives m(Cₖ) ≍ log k uniformly in k, and proves their Conjecture 9.2.1 for every odd integer n > 1. The proof combines Jensen’s formula, an elementary count of balanced quadruples of roots of unity, and the classical second-moment tail inequality. Only the second and fourth moments of the associated Laurent polynomial are needed; no independence among its monomials is assumed.
abstract_tex: Let \(C_k\) be the cyclovariety associated with all \(k\)-th roots of unity in the construction of Cornelissen, Hokken and Ringeling. title: Uniform stability of approximately idempotent laws on finite groups
abstract: For every C > 2, a probability law on a finite group with sufficiently small self-convolution defect is within C times that defect of the uniform law on a subgroup, in full ℓ¹ norm. The threshold depends only on C, independently of the group, and no symmetry or commutativity assumption is required. The coefficient 2 cannot hold at any universal positive threshold. The proof obtains approximate stochastic factors from the corrected small-projection theorem of Zippin, then uses translation invariance to recover an exact permutation action and a partition into subgroup cosets. A local estimate converts this coarse approximation into the linear bound. We give an explicit sufficient threshold for C = 4 and separate the nonabelian reconstruction from the abelian consequence of Saeki’s norm-gap theorem.
abstract_tex: For every \(C>2\), a probability law on a finite group with sufficiently small self-convolution defect is within \(C\) times that defect of the uniform law on a subgroup, in full \(\ell^1\) norm. The threshold depends only on \(C\), independently of the group, and no symmetry or commutativity assumption is required. The coefficient \(2\) cannot hold at any universal positive threshold. The proof obtains approximate stochastic factors from the corrected small-projection theorem of Zippin, then uses translation invariance to recover an exact permutation action and a partition into subgroup cosets. A local estimate converts this coarse approximation into the linear bound. We give an explicit sufficient threshold for \(C=4\) and separate the nonabelian reconstruction from the abelian consequence of Saeki’s norm-gap theorem.
teaser: On a finite group, a probability law with a small self-convolution defect is close to the uniform law on a subgroup. The threshold is uniform across finite groups.

title: A local-degree entropy bound for systematic Gibbs scans
abstract: Let P₁, …, Pₙ be the single-site heat-bath operators of a finite probability law. Suppose that Entµ(g²) ≤ L Σᵢ ‖(I − Pᵢ)g‖²₂ and that each update fails to commute with at most Δ others. We prove that every ordered sweep contracts entropy by a factor at most LΔ²/(1 + LΔ²). Approximate tensorization with constant C and a lower bound b on positive full one-site conditional probabilities gives L = C[2 + 2 log(1/b)]. The estimate permits constrained support and prescribed orders that vary between sweeps. Only full one-site conditional probabilities are bounded below; no lower bound under arbitrary partial conditioning is required. The proof follows square roots of the evolving densities, bounds their terminal local residuals using commutation, and charges their squared movement to entropy loss. Applied to the established fully frustrated hypercube Ising model with n = 2d sites and fixed inverse temperature 0 < a < 1/2, the estimate gives Oₐ(d^(5/2) log(n/ε)) complete sweeps from every starting state, uniformly over prescribed update orders. We compare this conclusion with consequences of earlier proofs and with the faster bound available for a chosen checkerboard order.
abstract_tex: Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) be the single-site heat-bath operators of a finite probability law. Suppose that \(\operatorname{Ent}_{\mu}(g^2)\le L\sum_i\lVert(I-P_i)g\rVert_2^2\) and that each update fails to commute with at most \(\Delta\) others. We prove that every ordered sweep contracts entropy by a factor at most \(L\Delta^2/(1+L\Delta^2)\). Approximate tensorization with constant \(C\) and a lower bound \(b\) on positive full one-site conditional probabilities gives \(L=C[2+2\log(1/b)]\). The estimate permits constrained support and prescribed orders that vary between sweeps. Only full one-site conditional probabilities are bounded below; no lower bound under arbitrary partial conditioning is required. The proof follows square roots of the evolving densities, bounds their terminal local residuals using commutation, and charges their squared movement to entropy loss. Applied to the established fully frustrated hypercube Ising model with \(n=2^d\) sites and fixed inverse temperature \(0<a<1/2\), the estimate gives \(O_a(d^{5/2}\log(n/\varepsilon))\) complete sweeps from every starting state, uniformly over prescribed update orders. teaser: The paper bounds how much entropy a full Gibbs sweep can retain, using a functional inequality and the number of updates that fail to commute. The bound holds for every prescribed order.

title: A dimension-independent box bound from dual total correlation
abstract: Let S be a finite nonempty set in a product of d coordinate spaces, and let Uₛ be its uniform law. We prove that some nonempty Cartesian box B satisfies |S △ B| ≤ 10 DTC(Uₛ)|S|, where dual total correlation is computed using natural logarithms. The constant does not depend on the dimension or on the coordinate alphabets. The proof follows actual coordinate slices: their average disagreement is bounded linearly by mutual information, while an exact entropy identity retains the deficit available within each slice. Selecting one slice with both costs controlled makes the induction close with the same constant. The resulting Loomis–Whitney stability estimate has coefficient 20(d − 1) under the usual normalized near-equality assumption. A two-point example shows that linear dependence on d is necessary in that normalization. The constants are not claimed sharp.

title: Dimension-independent stability of the real Böttcher–Wenzel inequality
abstract: The Böttcher–Wenzel inequality bounds the squared Frobenius norm of the commutator of two Frobenius-unit matrices by two. Its real equality cases consist of pairs supported on a common two-dimensional subspace, with traceless, orthogonal restrictions. We give a direct proof that a real pair whose squared commutator norm is 2 − δ lies within C√δ of such an equality pair, where C is independent of the matrix size. The distance uses the product Frobenius norm, neither matrix is required to be symmetric or normal, and no smallness assumption is imposed on the deficit. The exponent 1/2 is optimal, already in dimension three. The proof begins with Audenaert’s singular-value refinement, which provides a common subspace of dimension at most eight on which both matrices can be compressed. The retained commutator is orthogonal to the terms linear in the compression errors, so the normalized compressed pair has deficit of order δ. The remaining fixed-dimensional estimate follows from an explicit second-variation calculation: the deficit grows quadratically in directions transverse to the equality set. Compactness completes this estimate, and the compression argument combines only the constants for dimensions two through eight. The resulting universal constant is existential.

title: Local return moments and certified random-solving times for Rubik's Cube
abstract: Consider the random walk on the standard 3 × 3 × 3 Rubik’s Cube that independently chooses one of the eighteen face turns with equal probability. Let N denote the number of legal configurations and let Tₑ be the first hitting time of the solved configuration, including time zero. We give the certified bounds 1.0728316 < EπTₑ/N < 1.0729459. The same outward-rounded interval holds for EₓTₑ/N for every configuration whose face-turn distance from solved is at least thirteen. The proof combines the established Green-function hitting-time identity with a degree-six polynomial resolvent certificate, exact return-word counts through length twelve, and a symmetry-averaged diameter estimate giving a spectral gap of at least 1/600. The return counts were previously published in OEIS A061713 and are reproduced here by two independently implemented enumerations; all final inequalities use rational arithmetic. The certificate uses the classical matrix-moment framework to obtain an explicit finite-cube bound without computing the full spectrum or simulating rare solutions.

title: Partial Gaussian splitting in quadratic Wasserstein distance
abstract: Let µ = e^(−V) dx be a smooth probability measure on ℝⁿ with ∇²V ⪰ Iₙ. For 1 ≤ k ≤ n, suppose that u₁, …, uₖ are centered, variance-one Sobolev functions whose k gradients are orthogonal in L²(µ), and let D = Σᵢ(∫|∇uᵢ|² dµ − 1). We prove that there is a k-dimensional subspace E for which the squared quadratic Wasserstein distance from µ to the product of a standard Gaussian on E, translated by the projected mean, and the actual marginal of µ on E⊥ is at most 15D. The estimate has no ambient-dimension factor and requires no smallness assumption on D. The proof combines the Caffarelli contraction and Gaussian near-affinity estimates with a simultaneous selection of k directions and an explicit coupling that preserves the complementary marginal.
abstract_tex: Let \(\mu=e^{-V}\,dx\) be a smooth probability measure on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\nabla^2V\succeq I_n\). For \(1\le k\le n\), suppose that \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) are centered, variance-one Sobolev functions whose \(k\) gradients are orthogonal in \(L^2(\mu)\), and let \[D=\sum_{i=1}^k\left(\int|\nabla u_i|^2\,d\mu-1\right).\] We prove that there is a \(k\)-dimensional subspace \(E\) for which the squared quadratic Wasserstein distance from \(\mu\) to the product of a standard Gaussian on \(E\), translated by the projected mean, and the actual marginal of \(\mu\) on \(E^\perp\) is at most \(15D\). The estimate has no ambient-dimension factor and requires no smallness assumption on \(D\). The proof combines the Caffarelli contraction and Gaussian near-affinity estimates with a simultaneous selection of \(k\) directions and an explicit coupling that preserves the complementary marginal.
teaser: Nearly extremal directions for the Poincaré inequality yield an approximate Gaussian factor in quadratic Wasserstein distance. The estimate has no ambient-dimension factor.

title: Recovery of shared-cubic hidden-star networks from two differential boundary responses
abstract: Consider a network with labelled boundary terminals and unobserved interior vertices, each connected to every terminal, with no other edges in the network. On an edge incident to interior vertex c, the current law is a_ci(v + λ_c v³), where a_ci > 0 and the positive ratio λ_c is shared by all edges at that vertex. For two or more interior vertices, the differential boundary response at zero has a continuous ambiguity in the conductances. We prove that the response at zero together with the differential response at one nonzero, single-terminal bias determines all conductances and cubic ratios up to permutation of the interior vertices. The sufficient conditions are full column rank of two boundary-profile matrices and distinct component ratios in a matrix pencil. For a fixed nonzero bias, these conditions hold on an open dense set of full measure when each profile block has at least as many terminals as interior vertices. The proof combines differential-conductance reduction and established simultaneous diagonalization with an explicit recovery of physical scales. A two-center, five-terminal example illustrates every stage of the inverse. The result concerns exact differential data and the stated cubic network class; it makes no uniform stability or optimal terminal-count claim.
abstract_tex: Consider a network with labelled boundary terminals and unobserved interior vertices, each connected to every terminal, with no other edges in the network. On an edge incident to interior vertex \(c\), the current law is \(a_{ci}(v+\lambda_c v^3)\), where \(a_{ci}>0\) and the positive ratio \(\lambda_c\) is shared by all edges at that vertex. For two or more interior vertices, the differential boundary response at zero has a continuous ambiguity in the conductances. We prove that the response at zero together with the differential response at one nonzero, single-terminal bias determines all conductances and cubic ratios up to permutation of the interior vertices. The sufficient conditions are full column rank of two boundary-profile matrices and distinct component ratios in a matrix pencil. For a fixed nonzero bias, these conditions hold on an open dense set of full measure when each profile block has at least as many terminals as interior vertices. The proof combines differential-conductance reduction and established simultaneous diagonalization with an explicit recovery of physical scales. A two-center, five-terminal example illustrates every stage of the inverse. title: Arboreal height of integer-interlaced cubic squares
abstract: The arboreal height of a totally real algebraic integer is the least height of a finite rooted tree having it as an adjacency eigenvalue. Let α = λ² be a totally positive algebraic integer of degree three, and suppose that each open gap between consecutive conjugates of α contains an integer. We prove that λ has arboreal height at most three. Together with Schaeffer’s height-two criterion, this gives exact height two when the minimal polynomial of α has a root modulo two, and exact height three otherwise. The proof uses interpolation to express additive inverses as finite nonnegative integer combinations of star resolvents. Salez’s affine identity supplies inverses at the next branching level, where a cubic polynomial identity completes the construction. All intermediate branches are invertible at the prescribed eigenvalue. A dilation corollary determines the height of every sufficiently large integer multiple of a square root of an arbitrary totally positive cubic algebraic integer.

title: Arithmetic profiles and the prime spectrum of the integer necklace ring
abstract: Let R = Nr(ℤ) be the integer necklace ring and let B = ∏ₙ≥1 ℤ be its ghost product. We study ideal radicals and the ordinary prime spectrum through this embedding. For every ideal I ⊆ R, we prove (IB ∩ R)² ⊆ I. It follows that radicals contract and every prime of R lifts to B. We characterize the coordinatewise gcd profiles of finite ghost families by truncated valuation conditions and show that two ghosts realize every such profile. Consequently every finitely generated ideal of R has arithmetical rank at most two. The profiles give an arithmetic presentation of the lattice of quasicompact Zariski opens and of the spectrum, including specialization and the patch topology. A least compatible multiple construction gives infinitary divisibility criteria for equality and containment of ambient prime contractions. We also classify the primes closed in the necklace coordinate topology and describe all ambient primes above each of them. The resulting account distinguishes the full ordinary spectrum from its coordinate-topology-closed part and relates both to the known positive-characteristic and p-adic constructions.

title: A uniform logarithmic lower bound for cyclovariety Mahler measures: Expanded mathematical exposition
abstract: For the cyclovarieties Cₖ of Cornelissen, Hokken and Ringeling, we prove m(Cₖ) ≥ (1/6) log k − 1/4 + 1/(3k) − 1/(12k²) for k ≥ 2. Together with the known upper bound, this gives uniform logarithmic growth and proves their Conjecture 9.2.1 for every odd integer n > 1. This exposition develops the proof from its algebraic, analytic and probabilistic ingredients. We explain how cyclotomic coordinates preserve additive relations, derive the extra-variable Jensen identity with its integrability justification, count the second and fourth moments exactly, and obtain both a uniform comparison and the explicit lower bound. The monomials may be dependent. Figures illustrate the exact constructions and estimates; no numerical experiment is used as evidence for the theorem.

title: Near-uniform sampling of factored smooth integers in expected polynomial time
abstract: Given integers 2 ≤ y ≤ X, we consider the generation of an integer chosen nearly uniformly from the y-smooth integers at most X, together with its complete prime factorization. We give an unconditional algorithm using fair random bits whose output law is within total variation 2^(−h) of uniform and whose expected bit complexity is bounded by a fixed polynomial in ⌈log₂ X⌉ + h, uniformly in y. The algorithm requires no prime list, smooth-number counting oracle, saddle-point evaluation or general integer-factorization routine. Its construction combines tilted independent geometric prime exponents with sparse proposals over dyadic integer intervals. An explicitly filtered grid contains a useful tilt without computing it. Uniform smooth-number estimates give polynomial acceptance, and certified finite-precision primitives preserve both the distributional guarantee and the expected work bound. Every returned integer and its displayed prime factorization are exact; the approximation concerns only the sampling distribution. The guarantee concerns expected bit complexity; no practical running-time comparison is asserted.

title: Deterministic gaps between positive factorization cost and the entrywise norm
abstract: For a positive-semidefinite matrix, the sum of the squared ℓ₁ norms of its positive rank-one factors is at least the entrywise absolute sum of the matrix. We construct rational orthogonal projectors for which the minimum factorization cost exceeds this lower bound by a growing factor. Applying the deterministic almost Euclidean subspaces of Guruswami, Lee and Razborov gives an algorithm using polynomially many bit operations in the matrix dimension n, with ratio at least √n exp[−O(log log n · log log log n)]. The estimate holds for both real and complex factorizations. The proof uses the fact that positivity confines every factor to the projector range, together with a trace estimate; complexification preserves the subspace inequality without loss. An elementary construction from additive characters of the cubic graph over F_q, where q = 2^s, gives rank-q projectors in dimension q² with ratio at least √q/3. These elementary projectors also specify a rational positive operator with absolutely summable entries for which every countable positive rank-one factorization has infinite total squared ℓ₁ cost.
abstract_tex: For a positive-semidefinite matrix, the sum of the squared \(\ell_1\) norms of its positive rank-one factors is at least the entrywise absolute sum of the matrix. Applying the deterministic almost Euclidean subspaces of Guruswami, Lee and Razborov gives an algorithm using polynomially many bit operations in the matrix dimension \(n\), with ratio at least \(\sqrt n\exp[-O(\log\log n\,\log\log\log n)]\). The estimate holds for both real and complex factorizations. The proof uses the fact that positivity confines every factor to the projector range, together with a trace estimate; complexification preserves the subspace inequality without loss. An elementary construction from additive characters of the cubic graph over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q=2^s\), gives rank-\(q\) projectors in dimension \(q^2\) with ratio at least \(q^{1/2}/3\). These elementary projectors also specify a rational positive operator with absolutely summable entries for which every countable positive rank-one factorization has infinite total squared \(\ell_1\) cost.
teaser: Explicit rational projectors show that the cost of a positive rank-one factorization can exceed the entrywise matrix norm by a growing factor.

title: Recovery without a declining opponent: a two-state model motivated by the uncanny valley
abstract: An improvement in overall affinity need not mean that an unsettling response has declined: a positive contribution may instead come to outweigh a growing opponent. This note examines that possibility in a bounded two-state model motivated by the uncanny valley. It distinguishes Mori's appearance continuum from the evolution of a response during a fixed exposure. With separate positive rates for acquisition, loss, opponent recruitment and removal, both states increase from a neutral start. Their ratio is strictly increasing when ab ≤ (a + d)² and has one maximum when ab > (a + d)². In the latter regime, a defined interval of observation weights produces an initial rise, a negative excursion and a return above baseline. A worked example and a complete proof describe how this reversal of relative dominance occurs. A comparison with two real linear decay modes establishes a limited response distinction without selecting a unique mechanism. The measurement analysis also separates parameter uniqueness from prediction: exact opponent and mixed-response traces determine the reduced dynamics despite an unresolved scale of the positive component. The state architecture and general mathematical methods have established precedents, which are identified explicitly. The result is a conditional account of what this model permits, with synthetic illustrations and no participant experiments or empirical parameter fits. It does not establish that the latent components describe human familiarity or eeriness.
